preamble: Theatricals all have the same source

clue.text: Theatrical sound of horn on Paris street — request eggs for fox to eat

definitions.note: stands for a noun here: one of the theatricals, the plays the preamble says share one source

parts.note: a car horn's sound is a toot
rue is French for street

indicators.note: one piece eats another when it takes it inside, so the fox's letters surround the rest

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox
to beg is to make a request
O is egg-shaped, so two eggs give OO

explanation.surface: A jumble of Parisian street noise and a fox eating eggs it begged for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' signals that the fox swallows the request and the eggs. The theme is plays by George Bernard Shaw: this is one of his late comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A late comedy written by George Bernard Shaw, the common source of all the theatricals in this puzzle.

clue.text: Theatrical (if 3's) hell — abandoning love, police are wanted

definitions.note: a Shaw play whose title needs 3-down's answer in the possessive in front of it

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hence hell

indicators.note: the word police must give up one letter before its remaining letters are used
wanted here suggests the letters are needed in a fresh order, signalling an anagram

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shown as O

explanation.surface: A hellish scene where police are summoned once love has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops the O (love) from POLICE, and 'are wanted' rearranges the rest, PLICE, into CIPLE. 3-down gives the play The Devil's Disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil's Disciple is a Shaw melodrama, so with 3-down's word in front this follower completes the title.

clue.text: Was up to cook

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to have lived is to have existed, so was can be lived

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a person had been doing in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIVED in this down light. 'Was up to' looks like a single phrase about mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil food is to cook it with hot spicy seasoning, as in devilled kidneys.

clue.text: Leaves author on line

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A writer departs on a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage, the mass of leaves on plants.

clue.text: Northeastern town welcoming, if put before pet

indicators.note: the answer is what would go in front of the word pet to make the welcoming phrase, so pet is taken away

parts.note: red-carpet treatment is a lavish welcome, so welcoming suggests red carpet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern town is friendly if you bring your pet along first.
explanation.walkthrough: Red carpet, the lavish welcome, is the answer followed by PET. REDCAR is a seaside town on the north-east coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a town on the coast of north-east England, in North Yorkshire.

clue.text: Theatrical dwarf cut short by a beast

definitions.note: stands for a noun here: one of the theatricals, the plays the preamble says share one source

indicators.note: something cut short loses its last part, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a pygmy is a very small person, a dwarf
a lion is a wild beast

explanation.surface: A small person is overshadowed by a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final Y of PYGMY to leave PYGM.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's comedy about a phonetics professor transforming a flower girl, the basis of My Fair Lady.

clue.text: Successor to Michel, who deputised in Vienna

definitions.meaning: the name following Michel in Michelangelo, the Renaissance artist
the deputy who rules Vienna in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure

explanation.definitionFit: The second half of Michelangelo's name, and the deputy ruler in Measure for Measure, set in Vienna.

clue.text: Theatrical clue to earth the audience

definitions.note: stands for a noun here: one of the theatricals, the plays the preamble says share one source

parts.note: a heart broken up gives the letters of earth, so the first word read as an anagram clue would lead to earth
a house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A play hinting at the earth to the people watching it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read HEART BREAK as a little clue: break up HEART and you get EARTH. Shaw's play is Heartbreak House.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a Shaw play set in a country house during the First World War.

clue.text: Oil producer gets round to check about entering situation

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the two short words go into the word for situation

parts.note: the lie of the land is its situation
to vet is to check
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An oil supplier sends someone round to inspect the state of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the check and the about going into the word for situation; 'Oil producer' sounds like a refinery or a well.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is pressed from the fruit of this tree, so it produces oil.

clue.text: "Carry On" gems include Charlotte

indicators.note: the words include the answer, which runs across them

explanation.surface: The Carry On films are full of gems featuring a woman called Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' signals letters running through 'Carry On gems'. Charlotte M Yonge was a popular Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Mary Yonge was a prolific Victorian novelist, best known for The Heir of Redclyffe.

clue.text: Touchy creature back on the rooftop?

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: a cat is a creature
a tile is what lies on a roof

explanation.surface: A nervous animal turns back up on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAT into TAC. The surface suggests a cat on a hot tin roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to touch, so a crossword can call it touchy.

clue.text: Fellow MC's tail's in a twist

indicators.note: only the end of the word is twisted round, so its last pair of letters swap places

parts.note: a compere is a master of ceremonies, an MC

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies gets flustered at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail's in a twist' turns only the last two letters of COMPERE: RE becomes ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is an equal or companion, a fellow.

clue.text: I'm not sure I have a turn of speed!

definitions.meaning: a grunt of doubt or hesitation, a variant of humph
energy or zip, a variant spelling of oomph

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether they can still run fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses doubt like humph, and as a noun it is a spelling of oomph, vigour.

clue.text: Crude weapon wielded by pleb or mob around junction

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the junction letter
the words are brandished about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: a T-junction gives T

explanation.surface: A rough weapon brandished by a rabble near a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wielded' rearranges the rabble's three words, and 'around' puts the junction letter in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrol bomb is a bottle of petrol with a wick, a crude improvised weapon.

clue.text: Profligacy not allowed, they say in the belt

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the letters entered match how the phrase sounds

parts.note: profligacy is waste, and not allowed means banned

explanation.surface: A ban on extravagance applies to the belt-tightening economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals that 'waste banned' is heard rather than spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A waistband is the strip of fabric at the waist of trousers or a skirt, acting as a belt.

clue.text: The people about to knock the treatment

indicators.note: the word for people goes about the other piece

parts.note: they means the people in general
to rap is to knock

explanation.surface: Folk are about to criticise the medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the container signal. 'knock' also means criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal a disorder.

clue.text: Cheer for maturity by gardening establishment?

parts.note: to root for a team is to cheer for it
age means maturity

explanation.surface: Applause for a garden centre's seniority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardening establishment' looks like a garden centre; it means a plant becoming established by its roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootage is the taking of root, the way a plant becomes established in the garden.

clue.text: 4's author, upset about commercial, has changed sides

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: the author in 4-down is Graham Greene
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A novelist, annoyed by an advertisement, defects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges GREENE with AD; 'about' just links the commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is someone who deserts to the other side, a turncoat.

clue.text: A funny girl in bed

parts.note: rum means odd, funny
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An odd young woman is lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bed' sounds like sleep; it means a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a plant grown in a garden flower bed.

clue.text: Theatrical convert finds money at spring …

definitions.note: the captain converted in a Shaw play's title

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A stage convert comes into cash as the spring begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw wrote Captain Brassbound's Conversion. 'where there's muck there's brass' leads on to 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Brassbound is the man converted in Shaw's play Captain Brassbound's Conversion.

clue.text: Brightness is the last word about copper

indicators.note: the closing word goes about the metal's symbol

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Shine is the final word on copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharpness of mind, so brightness in the sense of intelligence.

clue.text: Ironical assent about modern street system

indicators.note: the sarcastic reply goes about the word for modern

parts.note: oh ay, said sarcastically, agrees while doubting
new means modern

explanation.surface: A sarcastic yes about the newest traffic scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. A sarcastic 'oh ay' is a northern English way of agreeing while doubting.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way street system lets traffic move in one direction only.

clue.text: … and its accompaniment, in for participation and out for stables

definitions.meaning: the proverb says where there is dirt there is money, so it goes with brass
to join in a shared task is to ... in
to clean out a horse's stall is to ... it out

explanation.surface: Continuing on from money, a word that goes with joining in and with stable chores.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 19: brass is money, and 'Where there's muck there's brass' is a northern English proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is dirt, and the proverb pairs it with brass; muck in and muck out are everyday phrases.

clue.text: Initiate dandy into murder

definitions.meaning: to give a novice a first taste, as hounds are first given a kill
a fashionable young man about town

explanation.definitionFit: Blood as a verb is to initiate; a blood was a Regency dandy; and blood stands for killing.

clue.text: Sol followed by thunder causes complaint

parts.note: sol is the fifth note of the scale, G
thunder rumbles

explanation.surface: Sunshine followed by thunder leaves people moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sol' looks like the sun; it is the musical note, G.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumble is a complaint, a moan.

clue.text: I delay returning sign to scientist

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a lag is a delay
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for being slow to send an astrological sign to a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns I LAG into GALI.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist.

clue.text: Theatre taking party back, one gathered

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre stages a party in the back, and one person turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DO into OD; 'gathered' rearranges ONE into EON. Odeon is a British cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon, from the Greek for a building for music, is a name for a theatre or cinema.

clue.text: Theatrical associate of 6's beast also moved closer

parts.note: and means also

indicators.note: the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A stage character, partner of the lion, moves in closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges CLOSER. Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw; 6's beast is the LION of 6-down. Shaw wrote Androcles and the Lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Androcles befriends the lion in Shaw's play Androcles and the Lion.
